Your shuttle settles on the landing pad and is met by no one.

Rusted mount-points remain where weapons emplacements once loomed.

You can only imagine what happened to the small squad of Diktat conscripts that used to garrison this platform.

Your shuttle settles on the landing pad assigned by the bored local traffic-control officer.

Luddic banners festoon the rusted mount-points where weapons emplacements once loomed - starbursts, coiled ivy, abstract patterns in muted tones.

The combat-tuned sensor suite of your shuttle does detect the giveaway tick-tick of stray radiations from point-defense weapon munitions and power-sources, armed and ready, but tastefully hidden. The Knights are here.

The surrounding platforms are pitted and charred by street-level fighting with only makeshift repairs made by the locals who have re-occupied this precious 'dry' ground.

A pair of off-duty laborers eye you fearfully, then duck into the maze of suspended walkways creaking between the extraction rig and surrounding barge structures.

The heavy doors to the shrine - holed by particle beam fire (so you judge from long experience) - stand open enough to permit ingress by foot.

A pair of off-duty laborers eye you fearfully, then duck into the maze of suspended walkways creaking between the extraction rig and surrounding barge structures.

The heavy doors to the shrine - the Luddic and anti-Luddic graffiti makes it clear that this is, in fact, the place - stand open enough to permit ingress by foot.

It's been holed by a particle beam. A light weapon by ship-borne standards, you judge. Something a power-armor squad or light agrav sled could utilize...

The surrounding platforms, pitted and charred by street-level fighting, have seen extensive repair due to generous donations from far-flung bodies of the Church of Galactic Redemption. The locals have been quick to accept this charity, and have re-occupied this precious 'dry' ground. At least those who can fit themselves into the shape of this new Luddic society.

A pair of off-duty laborers eye you as they eat noodles, legs hanging off the suspended walkways creaking between the extraction rig and surrounding barge structures.

The heavy doors to the shrine - holed by particle beam fire (so you judge from long experience) - stand open enough to permit ingress by foot. The damage could have been patched, but perhaps it is seen as an object of contemplation.

Something to do with wrath and martyrdom, perhaps.

The antechamber of the shrine is empty, as lonely as a coffin that never embraced the corpse for which it was constructed.

The receiving hall is pocked and scorched by more weapons-fire. Lighter here. Handheld arms. Rusty pools of dank water on the floor mingle with suspicious rusty stains.

It smells of salt and rot and smoke.

An enormous hole opens to the dark sea below. You can hear the waves slap against exterior bulkheads, though muffled. Someone's left candles here, though they're cold and dark and have gathered small pools of water inside the divits burnt into the paraffin.

The antechamber of the shrine is warm and well-lit, and lined with patchwork repairs, the walls a hand-built mosaic of corroded metal, ceramic, and plastic.

After a moment you recognize that it is a mural executed in a palette of rust and ruin, a crudely rendered scene of nature - and there, Ludd, an ambigious figure suggested by a ragged silhouette. 

It smells still of salt and smoke, but handweave carpeting softens the receiving hall. 

Simon the subcurate greets you with a half-bow and an offering of the briny tea of Volturn.

Simon leads you through the shrine, humbly rebuilt in much the same form - and there, the enormous, ragged hole still opens to the dark sea below. You can hear the waves slap against exterior bulkheads.

Swarms and schools of small candles gather and flicker along the ragged portal. Prayers and memories of the lost.

Their flames outnumber the visitors who pray or whisper quietly; a few may even be off-worlders, judging by their suits and robes bereft of salt-stain.

The antechamber of the shrine is not quite empty, as a humbly-robed subcurate greets you with a half-bow, and a quiet word lost in the distorted susurration of waves and wind.

Your eyes roam over the interior of the receiving hall, noting the pocks and scorch of more weapons-fire. Lighter here. Handheld arms. Artfully arranged hull-patch plates form a walkway through the rusty pools of water mingling with suspicious rusty stains.

Under the incense, it smells of salt and smoke. A hint of rot.

You are met outside by a jittery-looking local laborer. Not one of the two, from before.

He puts his hands together and nods at you, watery eyes nervously darting to your bodyguards.

"Was a raid," he says. "The Sindies got some word somehow. They say some informer told 'em there was a weapons cache."

He makes a nervous glance over his shoulder, though he seems gain confidence as he revisit what is clearly the source of simmering anger.

"Never saw anything like that, but the Sindies, they shot their way in. Set demolition charges, pulled back, and blew it. Word is, Faithful were sheltering in the deeps, in the old access tubes. Some VSDC, but mostly just regular walkers."

He seems to gain confidence as he revisits a simmering anger.

"Never saw anything like that, but the Sindies, they shot their way in. Set demolition charges, pulled back, and blew it. Word is, Faithful were sheltering in the deeps, in the old access tubes. Some VSDC, but mostly just regular walkers."

"All dead. Must have been quick."

The laborer clutches their hands together again, like some instinct to pray.

"I... I should go, boss. We never met," he turns away, then pauses. "Ludd's peace to you."

The laborer disappears, leaving you and your bodyguards on the charred platform. A cold drizzle begins to fall.

"I... I gotta go, boss." They turn away, and pause to look back. "Ludd's peace to you."

The laborer disappears, leaving you and your bodyguards on the charred platform. A cold drizzle begins to fall.

The flight in your return shuttle is uneventful.

You are keenly aware of the thin envelope of technology protecting you from the ravages of vacuum and radiation.

You step forward over the plates, and see in the center of the platform's main deck an enormous hole which opens to the dark sea below. You can hear the waves slap against exterior bulkheads, though muffled. There is a collection of candles set here, some lit, others are dark, with water collected in the divits burnt into the paraffin.

The subcurate notes your gaze.

"Blessed peace," he says in a rough voice, though softly. "Would you like to light a candle for someone?"

Despite the somewhat threadbare robes of a subcurate, you note that the man could be a laborer, maybe a low-status tech. Weathered face, scarred hands.

"It was a raid," he says. "The Sindies... the occupiers got word, somehow. It's said an informer told them there was a weapons cache in the shrine."

He indicates with his chin - the hole, the sea. A conspicuous and heavy absence.

"I'm called Simon," he says with a glance at you. "Came back after the committee said things were over. Took care of the place. They gave me a title, robes. Guess I found the calling late in life."

"And that," he kicks a foot forward, "was the shrine."

He's quiet for a moment. But he wants to tell the story.

"As I hear it, the Sindies, they shot their way in. Set demolition charges, pulled back, and blew it. Word is Faithful were sheltering in the deeps, in the old access tubes. Some VSDC, but mostly regular walkers."

"Not any who was down there, no," he says. "But the whole district was full of VSDC at the height of the fighting."

"Are you looking for someone in particular?"

Simon gives you a look, then turns back to contemplating the missing shrine.

"Well, this is it."

Simon gives you a look, then turns back to his contemplation.

"Standfast was her name. Don't think people are quite agreed about whether she was down there or not. When it happened, I mean. Lots of folks went away, and lots came back after the... the resolution. We've been rebuilding."

He shrugs, hands still held together.

Simon gives you a look, then turns back to his contemplation.

"Don't think people are quite agreed about whether she was down there or not. When it happened, I mean. Lots of folks went away, and lots came back after the... the resolution. We've been rebuilding."

He shrugs, almost sheepish, hands still held together.

"I pray for her."
"This is it," he says.

The antechamber of the shrine is empty, as lonely as a coffin that never embraced the corpse for which it was built.

The receiving hall is pocked and scorched by more weapons-fire. Lighter here; handheld arms. Rusty pools of dank water on the floor mingle with suspicious rusty stains. It smells of salt and rot and smoke.

An enormous, ragged hole opens to the dark sea below. Nearly half the underside of this platform must be missing. You can hear the waves slap against exterior bulkheads. Someone's left candles here, though they've burnt out and gathered small pools of water inside the divits burnt into the paraffin.

"Was a raid," a voice says.

A muted high pitched keen replies; sonic mapping, and just the barest flicker of barely-visible laser sweep to show that your bodyguards have quickly discovered the source of the voice. A murmur of tactical chatter confirms its owner is unarmed.

A rough-looking laborer, maybe a low-status tech, steps from the shadows. His eyes are cast toward the hole in the floor.

"The Sindies got word somehow. They say some informer told 'em there was a weapons cache in the shrine."

He indicates with his chin - the hole, the sea. A conspicuous and heavy absence.
